Under the modern majority rule, the niece has no interest. The words "to cousin and the heirs of his body" would have created a fee tail at common law, but most states have abolished the fee tail and convert it to a fee simple absolute in the cousin. The grantor then kept no reversion to convey, so his later deed to the niece passed nothing. (At common law the niece would have taken the grantor's reversion, and a few states that make the cousin's interest a life estate with a remainder to his heirs would leave her only a reversion.)

CONFIDENCE: 82
